account:
Today I followed my appointments: office business, a market walk, lunch at home, the town accounts review, and tea with my neighbour at the dockside cottage. I am now due back at the office at half past four. I have a feeling that something may be happening without my knowledge, but I have not found concrete evidence of any unusual activity. The neighbour says the docks have been quiet and reports nothing unusual since returning home. I have no evidence of a bread shortage or trouble with local trade.

At the accounts review, the builder reported no confirmed defects from visual checks of the bridge, landing, and warehouse approach. Freight said the warehouse was empty and there were no confirmed orders; they offered delivery quotes and ferry services if given a specific authorized consignment. The innkeeper attended, but I could not make out their business despite asking. The builder and freight approached the innkeeper about repairs and deliveries, which appears consistent with seeking ordinary paid work, not evidence of a hidden scheme.

The accounts are incomplete: the secretary had not seen an accounts ledger and could not verify balances or commitments. I personally checked the treasury and found 128 emeralds. Outstanding commitments remain unverified, and I authorized no spending. The secretary recorded these facts, reminded me of appointments, and accompanied me to tea. I have seen no reason to accuse anyone or infer a secret purpose. My best understanding is that townspeople are pursuing their ordinary work while I still need better information about town finances and any business I missed hearing.
